title: GB Domestic Rules
whatItIs: GB domestic rules (Transport Act 1968) apply to most goods vehicles that are exempt from the assimilated rules. The limits: 10 hours of driving and 11 hours of duty in a working day.

keyFacts.text: Under domestic rules you MUST NOT drive for more than 10 hours in a working day, on or off the public road.
Duty MUST NOT exceed 11 hours in a working day. Days when you do not drive are exempt.

keyFacts: Drive 4 hours or less every day of a week? No duty limit that week.
A working day is the 24 hours from the start of duty. A week is Monday 00.00 to Sunday 24.00.

keyFacts.text: Keep a weekly record sheet if the vehicle needs an operator licence and you drive over 4 hours that day.

keyFacts: No set breaks or rest, but employers must give 'adequate rest'.

visual.caption: GB domestic rules compared with the assimilated rules

a.label: Driving (domestic rules)
points: At the controls, moving or stationary with the engine running
Maximum 10 hours in a working day

b.label: Duty (domestic rules)
points: All driving and other work for your employer, not rest or breaks
Maximum 11 hours in a working day

onTheTest.question: Under GB domestic rules, what is the most driving in a working day?
onTheTest.why: Domestic rules: 10 hours of driving and 11 hours of duty a day.

onTheTest.question: Under GB domestic rules, when must you keep a weekly record sheet?
options: Every day you drive any goods vehicle
When it needs an operator licence and you drive over 4 hours that day
onTheTest.why: Keep a weekly record sheet if the vehicle needs an operator licence and you drive over 4 hours that day.

traps: Domestic daily driving is 10 hours every day, not 9 hours with two 10-hour days.
Domestic rules apply only in GB: abroad, follow local rules.
Mixed with assimilated driving? GB limits still apply, and assimilated time counts towards them.
